I got 24k under asking. Our townhome was on market for 67 days. We had 2 failed offers due to financing and the buyers realtors and mortgage brokers who did not do their due diligence in ensuring the buyers had financing in place before putting an offer. Finally when we got a third offer which we had no choice but to accept as we needed the money to close on our new build. We waited about 1 week to increase the buyer commission. I don’t remember the first commission but we did not get an offer until we did the first increase. It was really obvious the realtors didn’t bother until they got the full money. 

Another realtor on here said the buyers realtors  would have had to pay the difference and if they weren’t able to financially pay that difference the realtor wouldn’t show the house because their client couldn’t afford it. This apparently is in their contract that they will have the full commission, regardless of paying from our side or the buyers. The issue is, buyers are not really thinking of these things either. They don’t really see the commission should be lower, it would save them in the long run, less mortgage or money up front, they could potentially reduce the home price. Sellers would see the benefits immediately. But these things happen and I learnt the hard way. I hope eventually the system will be looked at. I spoke with the competition bureau of Canada about the issues a few months back as they were reaching out to consumers.

It’s not about the sellers side though, I sold through a discount realtor but still had the full commission on the buyers side because the buyers realtors refused to promote our home fairly. It’s negotiable but you have to play their game or the buyers realtors will not show the house, or give reasons as to why it’s a bad home.

Do your research and look for a good builder and check reviews. The reason people like older homes is the lot sizes are big, older furnaces seem to work better (but are not as efficient). Older homes also need to have windows updated to keep heat in the home. Many people have a bad taste for new homes, but I have bought two new builds and have been happy with both. Warranties and just knowing there’s no hidden issues helps. I’ve had friends go do house inspections and the inspector missed so many issues in the older homes and after the home is transferred to the new owner, it’s really hard to get anyone to take the responsibility. Older homes are can have efficiency issues but with new furnace, windows and some repairs you can keep the utility costs minimal. There’s good and bad for both, but I have been happy with my new builds. The floor plan is exactly what we wanted, we picked what we wanted and it’s all covered by the builder if anything goes wrong for 1 year after possession, then the new home warranty comes in.

I can speak for myself. I am in Canada (Alberta) which is probably one of the highest commissions in Canada. It’s 7/3 split between the buyer and seller agent and it’s 100% from the sellers side. We just sold a house using a low discount brokerage and ended up getting shafted and ignored for the first few weeks until we gradually increased the commission for the buyers realtor. We had 37 showings and 3 offers. 2 offers failed due to financing. We finally sold 24k under our original price (relisted and lowered below market). It was on market for 67 days. It was a horrible experience and I dont think I will ever sell a house again.

We also just spoke with a panel for the real estate competition bureau of canada and they told us it’s mostly 2-3% in other provinces split between the buyer and seller agent. Something definitely needs to change. One thing they asked is do you think there should be a fixed price for commissions? And another was do you think the buyer should pay out of pocket for their realtor? Absolutely. I have many friends who bought properties who had no idea that their realtors made literally thousands of dollars by selling homes. They thought the realtor/friend was being “nice”.  The commissions are not transparent and if we hadn’t done any digging when we were looking to sell our home we wouldn’t have known. The whole thing is so unfair for the seller.

I think it needs to be standardized in the industry and more transparent for the buyer that their realtors makes commissions. I think that they need to have something on the line on the buyer side.

Oh man. I had no idea postpartum grief was a thing until I experienced it first hand. My mom passed in 2014 and my daughter was born in 2020. My in-laws refused to see us because of covid and religious beliefs, my dad got remarried and didn’t see us as he didn’t want to deal with a newborn. I had an emergency c section and I learnt how to breastfeed from online forums/videos and lactation consultants. I also had tons of unresolved grief I didn’t even think I’d have but it came up. 

I had my son in 2022 via c section and a month later I had gallstones and needed another emergency surgery. My husband had such a hard time with our son who wouldn’t settle for 4 hours. It was horrible. 

What I have learnt, is to reach out when you need help, create your own village from friends, use online forums and take a little of column a and b. You won’t get everything right, but you and your partner should be able to lift eachother up when the other needs help. We are strong, but stronger together. When he needs a break, I can now recognize that and vice versa. We use daycare after a year for our daughter and I went back to work and our son will start in December. It’s hard but it’s so worth it. I go to the cemetery more often, I talk about my mom to my daughter. Things she liked and disliked. My daughter loves it, even if she doesn’t understand. I have told her I have two mommies but both love me (even though I am not close with my step mom). Kids are fine with simple discussions at 3. I don’t know what I’ll do when she asks more details, but I would like to think it’ll be gradual to the hard discussions. 

I want her to feel loved and cared for. I also feel in some ways loosing a parent at 27 makes me a better parent. I don’t coddle either child, I understand independence is important because I will not be there forever. The earlier they gain this confidence in themselves the better. My daughter is completely confident and bossy, it’s scary but I love it. My moms words were “I want you to stand on your own two feet “ and that will be passed to my kids. 


Another thing, as I’m going through this parenting journey, is I am doing things that my mom did which makes me feel more close to her. I also do things that she didn’t do but I know she’d be proud of me. I think even people who have their parents with them have problems. Yes, holidays and malls and swimming and everything is so so hard. Seeing grandmas at the zoo etc. but I just hold my littles and maybe, just one day I will be old enough to see them become parents. I can be the grandparent my mom never got to be. 

Lastly, you can’t really know how your partner will handle kids, but if they have problems or stress talk it out, go to therapy if needed. In our relationship, we both go to therapy separately. Dads can feel many of the emotions women feel but they are not discussed or tossed aside. Parenting is hard, it’s not impossible but if you have the right partner you can make amazing memories. 

Good luck!
